newsitem.title: EGYPT: Nile cruiser lists, tourists and crew missing.
newsitem.headline: Nile cruiser lists, tourists and crew missing.

text.p: At least six Czech and Slovak tourists and up to 18 Egyptian crew members are missing after a cruise boat on the Nile river listed and took on water, officials said on Friday.

The boat, named as the Amira Jihan, was carrying more than 70 Czechs and Slovaks between the tourist resorts of Aswan and Luxor when the accident happened in mid-stream at 3.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Thursday, they said.
Different sources had varying figures for the number of people on board but one official said 77 out of 83 tourists were rescued, along with 38 out of 56 Egyptian crew members.
Another said 63 out of 77 tourists reached the shore and the other 14 were missing.
Earlier reports said the boat had either sunk completely or run aground but a senior official in Edfu, the nearest large town, said it had listed and taken on some water.

"We have rescued 63 tourists and brought them to Edfu. Local people went out in small boats and pulled some of them out through the windows but they can't work now because it is pitch dark," said the official, who asked not be named.
The accident took place opposite the village of al-Mufalsa, about 20 km (12 miles) north of Edfu and 580 km (350 miles) south of the Egyptian capital Cairo.
A policeman in Aswan, the provincial capital, said: "We think that while the captain was trying to dock the boat along the shore, the boat tipped over because of the strong wind."
The survivors were taken to Edfu hospital for the night, some of them with injuries, and those able to do so would travel to Aswan later on Friday, security sources said.
In October, dozens of people drowned when an overloaded ferry on the Nile capsized while taking them home from a funeral. That accident took place further north, in the province of Minya.
